summary.oneLiner: Salasar Techno Engineering is a vertically integrated infrastructure player with dominant positioning in telecom towers and power EPC, benefiting from India's massive grid modernization and 5G rollout. The upcoming Asia's largest galvanization plant will unlock high-margin monopole production, enhancing revenue visibility and margins.

one-line thesis: Salasar Techno Engineering is a vertically integrated infrastructure player with dominant positioning in telecom towers and power EPC, benefiting from India's massive grid modernization and 5G rollout. The upcoming Asia's largest galvanization plant will unlock high-margin monopole production, enhancing revenue visibility and margins.
financial scorecard: rev: +24.3% YoY; EBITDA: +39.54% YoY; PAT: not disclosed; orderbook: ₹1,435 Cr; netdebt: working capital limit ₹250 Cr + ₹50 Cr planned increase
guidance: EBITDA margins sustain 9-10%; revenue growth driven by order book execution and new galvanization plant; expects additional ₹50 Cr revenue from new plant in FY24; targets export expansion and railway electrification orders.
order book & pipeline: ₹1,435 Cr total: ₹1,243 Cr EPC; ₹88 Cr Towers & Poles; ₹100 Cr Heavy Steel Structures; ₹400 Cr Railway Electrification (under execution); ₹750 Cr Rural Electrification (under execution)
segment / subsidiary detail: Telecom: angle bar, tubular, monopole, rooftop, camouflage towers; Power: transmission/distribution towers, substations, monopoles; Railway: electrification EPC, bridges; Renewables: solar mounting structures, windmill towers; Heavy Steel: prefabricated buildings, industrial structures; Smart City: smart poles, camouflage poles
growth verticals / optionality: New galvanization plant enables monopole production for 400kV+ transmission lines; export potential to USA/Canada; rural electrification pipeline of ₹25,000 Cr; 5G tower demand doubling; railway capex of ₹1.07 Lakh Cr; monopole segment has low competition
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin: 9.01% in Q1FY24 (up 99 bps YoY); sustainable range 9-10%; new galvanization plant expected to improve margins via vertical integration and premium monopole pricing; cost advantage from Ramboll designs reduces material cost by 40% vs conventional towers
capex / expansion: New galvanization plant nearing completion (Unit 3, Hapur); capex funded via debt; plant imported from Germany/Italy; capacity to produce 3m diameter monopoles; total manufacturing capacity: 115,000 MTPA
capital allocation: Debt expansion: working capital limit increasing by ₹50 Cr to ₹300 Cr; no equity dilution planned; capex focused on galvanization plant; no dividend policy mentioned; reinvestment in capacity and export readiness
risks & watch-items: Execution delays in EPC projects; raw material price volatility; currency risk on exports; regulatory delays in international approvals (e.g., USA/Canada); competition from Valmont and Skipper; dependence on government tenders
management quality / tone: Confident, optimistic, and detail-oriented; strong emphasis on execution capability, margin sustainability, and technological edge; proactive on export and monopole opportunity; transparent on order book and capex; avoids overpromising on railway order capture
non-obvious takeaways: Rural electrification order of ₹750 Cr is localized near manufacturing units, reducing logistics cost and improving margins; monopole plant is not just capacity expansion but a product differentiation play with no direct Indian competitor; Ramboll design IP provides structural cost advantage not easily replicable

themes.title: Power transmission & renewable-evacuation capex
themes.need: Grid build-out to evacuate ~90 GW of new renewables is the broadest theme in the universe - pulling EHV/765kV transmission EPC, towers, conductors, OPGW, cables and HVDC. POWERGRID/ADANIENSOL TBCB pipeline plus state RDSS/underground-cabling capex (Rajesh Power 544291, OMPOWER) underpins multi-year visibility for EPC, tower (KP Green 544150, SKIPPER) and conductor/cable makers (KEI, RRKABEL, DYCL).
themes.driver: Fresh TBCB awards + execution ramp; EPC order inflows over next 1-2 quarters.

themes.title: Railway rolling-stock & component capex
themes.need: A ~INR2.65 lakh cr Railways capital outlay and a pending ~1-lakh-wagon tender ('anytime this year' per JWL) drive rolling-stock, wheelsets, springs, castings, bogie components and interiors - with deep import-substitution (Neetu Yoshi 544434 castings; Airfloa 544516 interiors; Concord 543619 electronics). TITAGARH/TEXRAIL/JWL lead wagons; RVNL/IRCON/GPTINFRA on rail EPC.
themes.driver: Indian Railways large wagon tender award (next 1-2 quarters); wheelset plant ramp; Vande Bharat / Kavach orders.

themes.title: Telecom & digital-infrastructure capex
themes.need: 5G monetization, FTTH and tower/fibre densification drive the connectivity cycle - and Q1FY27 repriced the optical leg outright. STLTECH booked order intake of INR 13,100cr in ONE quarter, 1.7x its entire FY26 order book, anchored by a multi-year $1.1bn hyperscaler deal running through FY29, taking the open order book to INR 18,618cr (up 2.4x QoQ) on revenue of INR 1,910cr (+87%) and EBITDA INR 397cr (+184%). It then raised guidance twice on the same call - EBITDA margin target from 20%-by-end-FY27 (already hit at 20.8% in Q1) to 23%, and Data-Center + Enterprise mix from 30% to 50% of FY27 revenue, after DC went from 1% of revenue in FY26 to 21%. The catch is supply, not demand: ex the anchor deal quarterly intake fell to ~INR 3,000cr from INR 7,000-8,000cr because 'we have to pick and choose the orders basis the capacity availability', with germanium and helium named as binding raw-material constraints. BHARTIARTL on ARPU + 5G; INDUSTOWER on tower rollout; SUYOG-tier on passive infra; GTPL/HFCL-tier on broadband + fibre; tariff hikes and rural FTTH are the near-term levers.
themes.driver: STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler ramp against germanium/helium supply constraints and the raised 23% margin / 50% DC-mix guides; tariff-hike flow-through; 5G/FTTH capex; tower tenancy adds.
